The word is cognate with Old High German werento (“guarantor”). The verb is derived from Middle English warrant, waranten (“to give protection; to protect, shield; to assure, pledge, promise; to guarantee”), from Anglo-Norman warantir, warandir, warentir, and Old Northern French warandir, warantir, variant forms of Old French guarantir (“to protect”) (modern French garantir), a Romance formation from the noun guarant: see above.

senses.definition: To make a particular action, decision, or feeling necessary, appropriate, or reasonable.

examples.en: The minor injuries did not warrant a visit to the emergency room.
examples.vi: Những vết thương nhẹ không đáng phải đến phòng cấp cứu.

senses.vi: biện hộ cho; biện minh cho; đáng

senses.definition: To officially promise or guarantee that something is true, certain, or of good quality.

examples.en: The car dealer warrants that the vehicle is in excellent working condition.
examples.vi: Đại lý xe hơi đảm bảo rằng chiếc xe đang trong tình trạng hoạt động tuyệt vời.

thesaurus.definition: provide adequate grounds to justify (a certain course of action)
stand behind and guarantee the quality, accuracy, or condition of

wiktionary.gloss: To guarantee (something) to be (of a specified quality, value, etc.).

examples: That tree is going to fall, I’ll warrant.
wiktionary.gloss: To guarantee as being true; (colloquial) to believe strongly.

examples: I am warranted to search these premises fully.
wiktionary.gloss: To authorize; to give (someone) sanction or warrant (to do something).

examples: Circumstances arose that warranted the use of lethal force.
wiktionary.gloss: To justify; to give grounds for.

idioms.gloss: To make a decision that dooms one to certain death.
